sn11.19:0.3: The Worship of the Teacher or Sakka's Worship
sn11.19:1.2: “Bhikkhus, once in the past Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed his charioteer Mātali thus:
sn11.19:1.3: ‘Harness the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds, friend Mātali. Let us go to the park grounds to see the beautiful scenery.’
sn11.19:1.4: ‘Yes, your lordship,’ Mātali the charioteer replied. Then he hamessed the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds and announced to Sakka, lord of the devas:
sn11.19:1.5: ‘The chariot has been harnessed, dear sir.
sn11.19:1.6: You may come at your own convenience.’
sn11.19:1.7: “Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation and worshipped the Blessed One.
sn11.19:1.8: Then Matali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:
sn11.19:2.4: is that spirit To whom you bow in worship?’
sn11.19:3.2: In this world with its devas,
sn11.19:3.4: He is the one whom I worship, Matali.
sn11.19:4.1: Those for whom lust and hatred And ignorance
sn11.19:4.4: These are the ones whom I worship, Matali.
sn11.19:5.1: For the removal of lust and hatred,
sn11.19:5.3: The trainees who delight in dismantling,
sn11.19:5.5: These are the ones whom I worship, Matali’
sn11.19:6.1: ‘Those are indeed the best in the world,
sn11.19:6.2: my lord Sakka, Those whom you worship,
sn11.19:7.4: The chief, climbed into his chariot.”
